content_metadata.description: The session focuses on the proposal to establish a United Nations Advisory Body for AI, discussing the ethical, practical, and global cooperation aspects needed for AI regulation and advancement.

qAndA.answer: To provide guidance to the international community on the ethical and responsible use of artificial intelligence, ensuring it benefits humanity.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the proposed UN Advisory Body for AI?

qAndA.answer: He highlights the need for proper regulation of data and AI technologies to prevent unethical practices.
qAndA.question: What concerns does Dr. Mishari Al-Mishari raise about AI development?

qAndA.answer: He proposes focusing on real-world use cases and developing auditable certifications to guarantee AI technologies meet ethical standards.
qAndA.question: What specific suggestion does Dr. Adrian Walker make for the Advisory Body's work?

qAndA.answer: It visually reinforces the importance of the Global AI Summit as a platform for international collaboration and advancement in AI.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the closing scene with the summit's logo animation?

qAndA.answer: The session reflects a sense of urgency and responsibility towards harnessing the potential of AI while mitigating its risks. The speakers are optimistic about the possibilities but also acknowledge the need for careful consideration and action to ensure ethical and beneficial outcomes.

with the creation of an advisory body, as stated in the Rodmap for Digital Corporation.
The Secretary General has proposed that the United Nations offer itself as a platform
to convene stakeholders for the government, private sector technical experts,
academic civil society, around the discussion around artificial intelligence
and figure out how best the international community can use this technology
for the benefit of all demand.
They wish this body to provide guidance to the international community
on artificial intelligence that is trustworthy, human rights based,
safe and sustainable and promotes peace.
How do we keep the entire world on the right path?
So I strongly support the UN's role in this,
and I think things that develop its global significance would be helpful in this advisory body.
Because most innovators do need very clear direction from governments
in order to introduce new products and services, world administrative radio conferences.
You can help get nations together to set standards.
And it's not a top-down process, it's a collaborative process.
But I think if the stakeholders involve corporations, governments,
educators, universities and so on, all pretty much took the UN's role for granted.
It was just part of the natural backdrop in 10 years.
It was just assumed to be part of the ecosystem.
That would be success.
It's kind of as natural as breathing to have the UN providing whatever guidance or support
is necessary to introduce these listening technology.
AI is an opportunity, AI is potential, we can grow the global economy with artificial intelligence.
However, it is very difficult for me to imagine how we could realize the full potential of
artificial intelligence without properly regulating the AI sector.
It's very important to understand what is ethical and what is not ethical in AI.
And to draw clear borders of ethical innovation and artificial intelligence.
So we can ensure that AI is properly employed towards the good of humanity.
I believe we should start focusing on how we go about establishing a government's body
for data and artificial intelligence.
We need to see the results of that dialogues as clear actions that are being adopted at the
international level. To me, this is what we've created the success of this address.
And we really want to embrace those opportunities, learn what works well,
while also, of course, taking careful note of all the risks which have been discussed.
And so I think this body should be looking both at the potential benefits and the risks,
which is an approach which has already been embraced by the Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation
in the UK, looking at both those possible advantages and disadvantages together.
That speaks to, I think, your topic that I suggest that in order to make progress broadly,
we actually need to go deep on a few different areas to really try to listen carefully
in particular use cases. So we should pick some use cases which are key,
timely topics right now, but will also help to inform us as we think more generally about other
topics, would actually, in order to get something going, would be to think about the five pillars
that have been established, trustworthiness, human rights, safety, sustainability,
promotion of peace, and to help work towards reliable certificates, in some sort of
auditable guarantees that technology satisfies these sorts of requirements, which will then
enable cross-border use of technologies to flourish.
